summary: zap.c:zap_updown is only partially implemented. The selected upward WAN_STRIKING use reaches the C falling-rock arm, which makes a rn2(3) decision and then applies helmet-aware damage, creates and stacks a rock, and redraws the square. The JavaScript implementation skips this and the other source arms in zap_updown, so this needs the complete C function port rather than a one-branch workaround.

source.branch: zap.c:weffects() sends an immediate directional zap with nonzero u.dz to zap_updown(). Within zap_updown(), WAN_STRIKING falls through with striking=true; when u.dz<0, rn2(3) is nonzero, the level is not air or water, the hero is not underwater, and the level is not the quest start, C prints the dislodged-rock message, rolls rnd(2) for a hard helmet or rnd(6) otherwise, calls losehp(Maybe_Half_Phys(dmg), ...), creates a rock at the hero square, learns its description with xname(), stacks it, and calls newsym().
functions: zap_updown() whole zap.c:3219-3410; js/zap.js:6173-6256 currently implements WAN_PROBING and generic pile/map handling but omits WAN_OPENING/SPE_KNOCK, WAN_STRIKING/SPE_FORCE_BOLT, WAN_LOCKING/SPE_WIZARD_LOCK, SPE_STONE_TO_FLESH, and the source-sensitive upward/downward effect branches.
callers: zap.c:weffects() at 3438-3445 calls zap_updown(obj) when an immediate wand or spell has nonzero u.dz.
js/zap.js:weffects() at 6258-6265 calls zap_updown(obj, state, random) through the same production dispatch.
dependencies: Reuse existing JS implementations for bhitpile, zap_map, update_mapseen_for, display_binventory, hard_helmet, losehp, mksobj_at, stackobj, newsym, hides_under, hideunder, and trap.js openholdingtrap/closeholdingtrap/openfallingtrap; preserve their return and noticed semantics.
closeholdingtrap() has a consumed C boolean result; JS returns {result, noticed}, so use result for the C branch and merge noticed into disclose.
openholdingtrap() and openfallingtrap() are already implemented; C discards their return values but passes disclose by pointer, so retain their state effects and merge their returned noticed flag.

dbridge.c open_drawbridge(), close_drawbridge(), and destroy_drawbridge() have no JS implementation. Their C return values are void/discarded from zap_updown; record note_unported for each and skip those calls unless the callee is separately ported under an approved scope.

The selected hard-helmet case relies on do_wear.c hard_helmet() and zap.c Maybe_Half_Phys() damage reduction; both need their exact current JS helper/state representations read before implementation. Do not infer that the helmet is hard from its object name.

evidence: Saved admission evaluation challenges/evaluations/admission-b151b2318fa82ab62868ad676c7f00823de614c0-v58.json reports 168/243 screens and 243/243 cursors matched, with 2859/2919 RNG calls matched. The first mismatch is at step 168 on key <; C starts the screen with A while JS leaves a space. The C call trace is rn2(3) in zap.c:zap_updown at line 3307; JS has rn2(5) at the corresponding trace position.

The source-traced recipe independently starts as a level-20 Wizard, wishes for a wand of striking and a dwarvish iron helm, wears the helm, then zaps upward with repeated zo< input. The selected mismatch occurs on the first upward zap after those actions.

Read upstream zap.c:3219-3410 in full. The C WAN_STRIKING/SPE_FORCE_BOLT case sets striking=true, falls through to the shared striking/locking logic, and enters the falling-rock branch only after its drawbridge branch fails. Its branch order is rn2(3), air/water/Underwater/quest-start gates, message, rnd(hard_helmet(uarmh) ? 2 : 6), Maybe_Half_Phys, losehp, conditional mksobj_at/xname/stackobj, then newsym.

Read the full existing JS zap_updown() and production weffects() path. JS contains no striking branch and does not test the upward falling-rock conditions; it returns disclose after the generic upward hide-under behavior. The call is already wired, so the missing behavior is the partial zap_updown implementation, not a caller dispatch error.

Current-base selected-case scan at 73d0a1a0403910c12bd8c2590b83757f7361abb9 reproduces the saved first mismatch exactly: screen 168 and C rn2(3)=2 at zap_updown(zap.c:3307) versus JS rn2(5)=0. Scanner output is preserved in .cache/A2-v58-ceiling-striking-scan.json. It also reports the unrelated existing sounds.c SoundAchievement gap.
